sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

toolsAdded.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: mcp__session__transform_data
toolsAdded.description:
Transform data files using a script and write structured output for datatable/spreadsheet blocks, or extract HTML content for html-preview blocks.

Use this tool when you need to transform large datasets (20+ rows) into structured JSON for display, or extract/decode content for rich previews. Write a transform script that reads the input file and produces an output file, then reference it via `"src"` in your datatable/spreadsheet/html-preview/pdf-preview/image-preview block.

**Workflow:**
1. Call `transform_data` with a script that reads input files and writes output
2. Output a datatable/spreadsheet block with `"src": "data/output.json"`, an html-preview block with `"src": "data/output.html"`, a pdf-preview block with `"src": "data/output.pdf"`, or an image-preview block with `"src": "data/output.png"`

**Script conventions:**
- Input file paths are passed as command-line arguments (last arg = output file path)
- Python: `sys.argv[1:-1]` = input files, `sys.argv[-1]` = output path
- Node/Bun: `process.argv.slice(2, -1)` = input files, `process.argv.at(-1)` = output path
- For datatable/spreadsheet: output must be valid JSON: `{"title": "...", "columns": [...], "rows": [...]}`
- For html-preview: output is an HTML file (any valid HTML)

**Security:** Runs in an isolated subprocess with no access to API keys or credentials. 30-second timeout.

Use this for short Python/Node/Bun snippets when strict Explore-mode Bash parsing blocks inline diagnostics.

- Returns stdout/stderr, exit code, duration, and timeout status
- Accepts optional input files and stdin
- Requires enforced network and filesystem isolation; if unsupported or unusable, execution is blocked

**Safety:**
- Sensitive credential env vars are stripped
- Input files are restricted to the current session directory
- Filesystem writes are restricted to the current session directory
- Timeout is capped (default 5000ms, max 15000ms)

toolsAdded.description:
Invoke a secondary LLM for focused subtasks. Use for:
- Cost optimization: use a smaller model for simple tasks (summarization, classification)
- Structured output: JSON schema compliance via prompt instructions
- Parallel processing: call multiple times in one message - all run simultaneously
- Context isolation: process content without polluting main context

Put text/content directly in the 'prompt' parameter. Do NOT pass inline text via attachments.
Only use 'attachments' for existing file paths on disk - the tool loads file content automatically.
For large files (>2000 lines), use {path, startLine, endLine} to select a portion.

Default fast model for this session: pi/deepseek-flash. Omit the model parameter to use it automatically.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__session__decide
toolsAdded.description:
Ask the decision model (Jev, TypeSafe System One) typed questions about text or JSON. It answers with probabilities, never prose: 'choice' picks one of your named options, 'score' places the state on an ordered rubric, 'noul' gives a yes/no probability. Fast (~0.1–0.5 s per call) and cheap; batch mode judges up to 200 items in one call.

Use it to classify, route, tag, rank or triage many items (emails, tickets, rows, search hits), for yes/no checks over a list, or to score against a rubric. Do NOT use it for anything that needs generated text, value extraction or reasoning — use call_llm for those.

Question design: short option keys with a one-sentence description each (null when self-explanatory); English instructions; score levels ordered lowest → highest; add an 'other' or 'unclear' option when the categories are not exhaustive. Ask several questions per call instead of several calls.

Read answers honestly: confidence below 0.5 means the model is unsure — say so or ask the user instead of acting on it; choose noul thresholds for the stakes (0.8+ when a false yes is costly). Answers are hints, never permission: re-check before acting on them.

Privacy: the state is sent to the user's configured decision provider (TypeSafe, OpenRouter, Vercel AI Gateway or their own server). Do not include secrets or content that must not leave the machine. Only available when the user enabled the decision model in Settings > AI.

state.description: What to judge: text, a JSON object, or an array of strings. Required unless items is given.

items.description: Batch mode: judge every item as its own state with the same questions (max 200). Results keep the input order.

type.description: 'choice' picks one of your named options, 'score' places the state on an ordered rubric, 'noul' answers yes/no with a probability.

instructions.description: The question, in English. One short sentence, or an object such as { question, focus }.

criteria.description: choice: object of option key → one-sentence description (2–255 options; null when the key is self-explanatory). score: ordered array of level descriptions, lowest first (2–10). noul: optional { true: '...', false: '...' } descriptions.

questions.description: Question key → question (max 20 per call). Keys are echoed in the answers.

deadlineMs.description: Time budget per call in ms (default 10000).

When spawning, the 'prompt' parameter is required.

Optional overrides: `model`, `llmConnection`, `permissionMode`, `thinkingLevel`, `enabledSourceSlugs`, `labels`, `workingDirectory`. Omitted fields inherit from the spawning session or the workspace default.

`thinkingLevel` is silently ignored on non-reasoning models (e.g. gpt-4o, gemini-2.5-flash) — the SDK drops the reasoning param rather than erroring. Use it when you want to force deeper reasoning on a supported model, or set it to `off` when spawning a session that doesn't need to think.

All browser interactions use this single tool with strict validation and actionable feedback.
String mode supports batching with semicolons: `fill @e1 value; fill @e2 value; click @e3`
Batch stops after navigation commands (click, navigate, back, forward) since page state may change.

Array mode bypasses string parsing and preserves raw arguments exactly (recommended for semicolons, tabs, and newlines):
- `["evaluate", "var x = 1; var y = 2; x + y"]`
- `["paste", "Name\tAge\nAlice\t30"]`

Examples:
- `--help`
- `open`
- `navigate https://example.com`
- `snapshot`
- `find login button` — search elements by keyword
- `click @e12`
- `click-at 350 200` — click at pixel coordinates (for canvas elements)
- `fill @e5 user@example.com`
- `type Hello World` — type into currently focused element (no ref needed)
- `select @e3 optionValue`
- `select @e75 CNAME --assert-text Target --timeout 3000`
- `set-clipboard Name\tAge\nAlice\t30` — write text to clipboard
- `get-clipboard` — read clipboard text content
- `paste Name\tAge\nAlice\t30` — set clipboard and trigger Ctrl/Cmd+V
- `scroll down 800`
- `evaluate document.title`
- `console 50 error`
- `screenshot` — raw screenshot
- `screenshot --annotated` — screenshot with @eN labels overlaid on interactive elements
- `screenshot-region 100 200 640 480`
- `screenshot-region --ref @e12 --padding 8`
- `screenshot-region --selector div[data-testid="chart"]`
- `window-resize 1440 900`
- `network 50 failed`
- `wait network-idle 8000`
- `key Enter`
- `key k meta`
- `downloads wait 15000`
- `focus [windowId]` — focus existing browser window (no new window)
- `windows` — list current browser windows and ownership state
- `release` — dismiss the agent control overlay when done
- `close` — close and destroy the browser window
- `hide` — hide the window while preserving state

# Win32 C++ style guide

This repository targets C++20 and the Windows SDK. These rules apply to the NEWAGEAI app and the reusable controls in `projects/implementing-win32-lego/assets/`.

## Source layout and naming

- Keep one public module API in its matching `.h` file and its non-inline implementation in the matching `.cpp` file. Use `#pragma once` and include the precompiled header first in project `.cpp` files.
- Put reusable controls in `namespace win32::controls`. Use `PascalCase` for types and public functions; use `camelCase` for parameters and locals. Preserve the app's `g_` global and `m_` member prefixes and its `k` prefix for named constants.
- Include the header that directly declares each dependency. Group project headers before standard-library headers where practical. Keep source files Unicode and use `W`-suffixed Win32 APIs and UTF-16 strings.
- Use four spaces, braces on their own line for functions and control blocks, and one statement per line in new or substantially edited code. Keep source files compatible with the project's Visual Studio C++20 settings. `.clang-format` and `.editorconfig` hold the editor defaults.

## Ownership and errors

- Treat every Win32 handle as either owned or borrowed. Owning wrappers are non-copyable and movable; `Reset()` destroys the owned resource and `Release()` explicitly transfers it. Never destroy borrowed handles.
- `ChildControl` owns the child `HWND` it creates. Its parent must outlive it; reset/destroy controls before destroying the parent. `Menu::AppendSubmenu` transfers the submenu to the parent menu on success. Image lists assigned to another control remain owned by their `ImageList` wrapper unless released.
- Validate parameters at public boundaries. Return `bool` for success/failure, `std::optional` where an empty value differs from failure, and document when a method returns a native Win32 previous-state/index value. Use the native Unicode API and message corresponding to the control.
- Parent windows remain responsible for routing control notifications. Owner-drawn controls require the parent to forward `WM_DRAWITEM`; split buttons notify through `BCN_DROPDOWN`; accelerators are translated by the app's message loop.

## Comments

- Write comments for public contracts, ownership/lifetime, required parent-window message handling, units, and non-obvious Win32 behavior—not to narrate each statement.
- Use `///` comments immediately above public types and APIs. Use concise `// ---- Section ----` headings for substantial implementation sections. Add a short inline comment only when it explains a non-obvious invariant or Win32-specific reason.
- Keep comments accurate when code changes. Prefer descriptive names and small functions over explanatory comments that merely restate the code.

## Example API documentation

```cpp
/// Owns an HIMAGELIST. The caller retains ownership of any HICON passed to AddIcon.
class ImageList final {
public:
    bool Create(int width, int height, UINT flags) noexcept;
    int AddIcon(HICON icon) noexcept;
    HIMAGELIST Release() noexcept;
};
```

## Build integration

Every `.cpp` implementation must be listed in `NEWAGEAI.vcxproj`; headers and sources should also appear under the matching `Win32 LEGO Controls` filter in `NEWAGEAI.vcxproj.filters`. Common-control classes must request their `ICC_*` initialization flags before creation. Link Win32 dependencies through the project settings (`comctl32.lib`, `uxtheme.lib`, `msimg32.lib`, and `winmm.lib`) rather than source-level linker pragmas.

content.text:
# NEWAGEAI

A Unicode Win32 C++ application and reusable-control template. Main-window
settings live in the `g_mainCfg` configuration in `Config.h`:

    WindowKind   Overlapped / FullScreen / CompactOverlay / Modal
    ThemeMode    System / Light / Dark
    DpiMode      Unaware / System / PerMonitor / PerMonitorV2
    ...

## Files

    main.cpp                app logic + the editable CONFIG block
    pch.h / pch.cpp         precompiled header
    Config.*                app configuration and theme values
    Button/*                reusable button drawing and management
    AboutWindow/*           configurable About window
    resource.h              resource IDs
    NEWAGEAI.rc             icon, string table, About dialog
    projects/implementing-win32-lego/assets/
                            reusable Win32 control modules
    WIN32_CPP_STYLE.md      C++ ownership, naming, and comment conventions
    .editorconfig           whitespace and line-ending defaults
    .clang-format           C++ formatter profile
    NEWAGEAI.vcxproj        MSBuild project and Win32 library links
    NEWAGEAI.vcxproj.filters
    README.md               this file

## Reusable Win32 controls

The modules under `projects/implementing-win32-lego/assets/` provide wrappers for
accelerators, date/time pickers, group boxes, headers, image lists, list boxes,
list views, menus, month calendars, owner-drawn controls, progress bars,
scrollbars, status bars, tabs, toolbars, split buttons, tooltips, trackbars,
tree views, and up-down controls. They use the `win32::controls` namespace and
are included in the Visual Studio project.

Include the module header you need, then create the control with its parent,
control ID, and client-area bounds. For example:

```cpp
#include "projects/implementing-win32-lego/assets/ListView.h"

// Keep the wrapper in the parent window's state, not as a short-lived local.
win32::controls::ListView list;
list.Create(hwnd, 2001, 12, 48, 520, 300);
list.InsertColumn(0, L"Name", 240);
list.InsertItem(0, L"Example");
```

The wrapper owns the child `HWND`; its parent must outlive the wrapper. The
parent still handles notifications. Owner-drawn controls require forwarding
`WM_DRAWITEM`, split buttons report `BCN_DROPDOWN`, and accelerator tables must
be translated from the message loop. See [WIN32_CPP_STYLE.md](WIN32_CPP_STYLE.md)
for ownership and commenting rules.

## Build

Open `NEWAGEAI.vcxproj` in Visual Studio 2022 (Desktop development with C++),
select `x64` / `Debug`, and press F5.

## Switch window kind (edit `g_mainCfg` in `Config.h`)

Standard overlapped:

    .kind = WindowKind::Overlapped,
    .width = 900, .height = 600,
    .minWidth = 400, .minHeight = 300,

Fullscreen (press Esc or Alt+F4 to close):

    .kind = WindowKind::FullScreen,

CompactOverlay / Picture-in-Picture:

    .kind = WindowKind::CompactOverlay,
    .compactOverlayPercent = 15,   // 5 = Small, 15 = Medium, 25 = Large

Modal (blocks its owner until closed):

    .kind = WindowKind::Modal,
    .owner = /* HWND of the window to disable */,
    .width = 400, .height = 300,

DPI mode:

    .dpiMode = DpiMode::PerMonitorV2,  // or System / PerMonitor / Unaware

Startup theme:

    .themeMode = ThemeMode::Dark,      // or Light / System

### 10.3 Registry Key Change

For backward compatibility, the standalone exe keeps `HKCU\Software\ModernNotepad`. The DLL does not touch the registry unless explicitly told to via a `LoadSettings`/`SaveSettings` export (added in v2 if needed).

---

## 11. Theme Coordination

### 11.1 Default Theme

The built-in dark theme (current `Theme::Palette`) is the default. It is copied into each `NotepadInstance` at creation time.

### 11.2 Custom Theme

`SetTheme(hPanel, &theme)` copies the provided palette into the instance and triggers a full repaint. Every paint function (`PaintTabs`, `PaintSearchBar`, `PaintStatusBar`, `DrawButton`, icon drawing) reads from `instance->theme` instead of the global `Theme::` namespace.

### 11.3 Light Theme Support

The color set is already well-structured (14 named colors). A light theme is just a different `NPTheme` struct:

```cpp
NPTheme light = {
    .bgApp      = RGB(255, 255, 255),
    .bgPanel    = RGB(248, 248, 248),
    .bgCard     = RGB(238, 238, 238),
    .bgBtn      = RGB(228, 228, 230),
    .bgBtnHi    = RGB(218, 218, 222),
    .border     = RGB(200, 200, 204),
    .borderSoft = RGB(220, 220, 224),
    .textHi     = RGB(28, 28, 32),
    .textMid    = RGB(100, 100, 108),
    .textLow    = RGB(150, 150, 158),
    .accent     = RGB(37, 99, 235),
    .selBg      = RGB(206, 224, 255),
    .iconIdle   = RGB(60, 60, 68),
    .iconActive = RGB(20, 20, 28),
};
SetTheme(hPanel, &light);
```

### 11.4 RichEdit Theme

`SetWindowTheme(hEdit, L"DarkMode_Explorer", nullptr)` is called for dark mode. For light mode, call `SetWindowTheme(hEdit, L"Explorer", nullptr)` and set `EM_SETBKGNDCOLOR` to the theme's `bgApp`.

### 11.5 DWM Dark Title Bar

# Adopt NEWAGEAI theme + Win32 C++ conventions in Neage Notepad

## Goal

Bring `D:\CPROJECTS\NEAGENOTEPAD` up to the standard set by the two reference projects:

1. **Theme** — implement NEWAGEAI's `ThemeMode` / `ThemeColors` model (System / Light / Dark, system- dark detection, DWM title bar theming, DPI scaling) as a real module in Neage Notepad.
2. **Programming style + commenting convention** — apply `NEWAGEAI\WIN32_CPP_STYLE.md` to every source file.
3. **Organization** — use `NEWAGEWIN32UI`'s one-component-per-`.h`/`.cpp` layout (Standard vs Advanced control tiers) as the rule for creating new modules, and document it.

No behaviour regressions: the public C API stays source- and binary-compatible, and the reformat is proven token-identical to the current code.

---

## What I found

### Reference: NEWAGEAI

`WIN32_CPP_STYLE.md` + `.clang-format` + `.editorconfig` define the convention:

| Rule | Reference implementation |
|---|---|
| Header layout | `#pragma once` → includes → `// ---- Section ----` → enums → structs → `///`-documented API |
| Public docs | `///` immediately above public types/functions, stating contract, ownership, units |
| Implementation sections | `// ---- Button Factory ----`, short, not `// =========` banners |
| Comments | Only for contracts, ownership/lifetime, required message handling, units, non-obvious Win32 behaviour — **never per-statement narration** |
| Formatting | 4 spaces, Allman braces, one statement per line, 100 col, UTF-16 `W` APIs |
| Ownership | Owned vs borrowed handles, `Reset()` / `Release()`, parent outlives child |
| Build | Every `.cpp` in `.vcxproj` + filters; libs in project settings, **not** `#pragma comment(lib, …)` |

Theme model lives in `Config.h`:

```cpp
enum class ThemeMode { System, Light, Dark };
struct ThemeColors { … };              // bg, text, caption, status, menu colours
inline ThemeColors GetThemeColors(bool dark);
```

with `ReadSystemDarkMode()` (reads `AppsUseLightTheme`), `ResolveTheme()` and `ApplyTitleBarTheme()` (`DwmSetWindowAttribute` 20→19, caption 35/36, border 34) in `main.cpp`.

### Reference: NEWAGEWIN32UI

`Controls/Standard/*` (common controls) and `Controls/Advanced/*` (owner-drawn/complex), **one type per header/cpp pair**, thin headers, implementation in the `.cpp`, reusable modules in `namespace win32::controls`.

### Target: NEAGENOTEPAD (current state)

| Problem | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Narration comments on almost every line | 2,579 of 2,742 lines in `NotepadPanel.cpp` carry `//`; 257× `// Close the current block.`, 132× `// Complete the current operation…`, 50× `// Supply this parameter…` |
| Wrong brace/format style | K&R braces, multiple statements per line (`wc.lpfnWndProc = …; wc.hInstance = …;`) |
| Banner style not in convention | `// ============================================================` |
| No theme module | `Palette` + `DefaultDarkTheme()` are file-static inside `NotepadPanel.cpp`; dark-only; `SetWindowTheme(hEdit, L"DarkMode_Explorer")` hardcoded |
| No system/light theme | No `ThemeMode`, no registry read, no light palette; `SetTheme(NULL)` always restores dark |
| No DPI/title-bar module | Inline `MulDiv` helper per file; `DwmSetWindowAttribute` inline in `NEWAGENOTEPADMain.cpp` |
| No PCH / style docs / formatter | no `pch.*`, no `WIN32_CPP_STYLE.md`, no `.clang-format`, no `.editorconfig` |
| Build drift | `NEWAGENOTEPADMain.cpp` missing from `.filters`; libs via `#pragma comment`; PCH unused |

`EMBEDDING_SPEC.md` §11 already specifies the intended end state (per-instance palette, light palette, `SetWindowTheme` per mode) — the code just never got there.

---

## Deliverables

### New files

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `WIN32_CPP_STYLE.md` | Project convention: layout, naming, comment rules, ownership, theme rules, "how to add a module" checklist (adapted from NEWAGEAI, includes the `Controls/Standard` vs `Controls/Advanced` organization rule from NEWAGEWIN32UI) |
| `.clang-format`, `.editorconfig` | Exact copies of the NEWAGEAI profiles (Microsoft base, Allman, 4 spaces, 100 col) |
| `pch.h`, `pch.cpp` | `NOMINMAX`, `WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN`, `_WIN32_IE`, `windows.h`, `<string>`, `resource.h` — reference convention |
| `Theme/Theme.h` | `ThemeMode`, `ThemePalette` (15 colours), `DarkPalette()`, `LightPalette()`, `GetPalette(ThemeMode)`, `IsSystemDarkMode()`, `ResolveDarkMode()`, `ScaleMetric()`, `ApplyTitleBarTheme()`, `ApplyControlTheme()` — all `///`-documented |
| `Theme/Theme.cpp` | Palette tables, registry read, DWM attribute application (20→19, 35/36/34), `SetWindowTheme` per mode. Sections as `// ---- Palette ----`, `// ---- System preference ----`, `// ---- DWM integration ----` |

### Modified files

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `NotepadPanel.cpp` | Remove narration comments, Allman reformat, one statement per line, `// ---- … ----` sections; use `Theme/Theme.h`; new theme-mode exports + View-menu entries |
| `NotepadPanel.h` | Comment cleanup to the reference block style; additive `NP_THEME_*`, `NP_CMD_THEME_*`, `NP_NOTIFY_THEME_CHANGED`, `SetThemeMode` / `GetThemeMode` with `///`-level contract docs |
| `NEWAGENOTEPADMain.cpp` | Convention rewrite; resolve system theme, apply title bar via `Theme`, react to `WM_SETTINGCHANGE`, use PCH |
| `Neage Notepad.vcxproj` | Add `Theme/Theme.cpp`, `Theme/Theme.h`, `pch.*`; enable PCH; move libs to project settings (`comctl32;comdlg32;shell32;dwmapi;uxtheme`); Common-Controls v6 manifest via project |
| `Neage Notepad.vcxproj.filters` | Add `Theme` filter; register `NEWAGENOTEPADMain.cpp` (currently missing), `pch.*`, `Theme/*` |
| `README.md` | Project map, conventions pointer, build steps |
| `NOTEPAD_PANEL_API.md` | Document `SetThemeMode` / `GetThemeMode`, theme-mode constants, new notification, revised `SetTheme(NULL)` semantics |
| `EMBEDDING_SPEC.md` | §11 rewritten to match the shipped `Theme/` module |

---

## Theme design

```cpp
enum class ThemeMode
{
    System = 0,   // resolve against AppsUseLightTheme at the moment of use
    Light  = 1,
    Dark   = 2
};

struct ThemePalette
{
    COLORREF BgApp, BgPanel, BgCard, BgBtn, BgBtnHi, BgRailHi;
    COLORREF Border, BorderSoft, TextHi, TextMid, TextLow;
    COLORREF Accent, SelBg, IconIdle, IconActive;
};
```

- **Dark** = the current `DefaultDarkTheme()` values (pixel-identical, no visual change).
- **Light** = the palette already specified in `EMBEDDING_SPEC.md` §11.3.
- `ThemePalette` keeps the existing PascalCase field names, so the ~40 paint sites keep `inst->theme.BgApp`.
- `NPTheme` (the C struct) is converted at the API boundary; `Theme` has **no** dependency on the public header.
- `SetTheme(NULL)` restores the palette of the instance's current theme mode (dark when unset) — documented change from "always dark".
- Panel default stays **Dark** for embedders (no visual surprise); the standalone app switches itself to **System**.
- RichEdit + rename edit use `ApplyControlTheme(hwnd, dark)`; the frame uses `ApplyTitleBarTheme(hwnd, dark)`.
- New exports: `SetThemeMode(HWND, int)` / `GetThemeMode(HWND)`, plus `NP_NOTIFY_THEME_CHANGED`.
- View menu gains `Theme: System / Light / Dark` with check marks (`NP_CMD_THEME_SYSTEM/LIGHT/DARK`, 2050–2052).

---

## Comment + format policy (the core of the request)

1. **Delete** all statement narration — the generated families
   (`// Close the current block.`, `// Call X to …`, `// Declare X and start with …`,
   `// Continue this branch only when …`, `// Return the computed … to the caller.`,
   `// Update the … field with the calculated value.`, …). 2,579 comment-bearing lines → roughly 120.
2. **Keep or rewrite** only comments that carry information: file headers, control-ID/MSG mapping notes, struct field group labels (`// Window handles`, `// Documents`), genuine invariants (`// Ctrl+W is close-tab, not exit`, `// no default key`, `// 30..500`), and Win32 reasons.
3. **Section headings** become `// ---- Name ----` (reference style), not `// ====`.
4. **Public contracts** are documented once, in the header, above the declaration.
5. **Formatting**: `.clang-format` applied (`clang-format -i`), plus a pass that splits `a; b; c;` into one statement per line (clang-format does not do this).
6. **Safety proof**: a token-normalizer compares the current and refactored `NotepadPanel.cpp` — comments/whitespace stripped, tokens must match exactly. Any unintended logic edit shows up as a diff.

---

## Execution phases

**Phase 1 — Convention files (zero code risk)**
`WIN32_CPP_STYLE.md`, `.clang-format`, `.editorconfig`, `pch.h`/`pch.cpp`, README structure section.

**Phase 2 — Theme module**
Write `Theme/Theme.h` + `Theme/Theme.cpp`, register in project, build standalone. No callers yet, so the app is unchanged.

**Phase 3 — NotepadPanel refactor (largest diff)**
Strip narration → merge `// ====` banners into `// ---- ----` → split multi-statement lines → `clang-format` → token-identity check → wire `Theme/` (palette, control theme, mode field, exports, menu entries) → build.

**Phase 4 — App + docs**
`NEWAGENOTEPADMain.cpp` on the theme module (system resolve, `WM_SETTINGCHANGE`, title bar, DPI helper); update API docs and spec.

**Phase 5 — Verification**
`MSBuild "Neage Notepad.vcxproj" /p:Configuration=Debug /p:Platform=x64` and `Release|x64`; fix warnings; confirm token diff and public export list (`dumpbin /exports`).

---

## Verification checklist

- [ ] Debug|x64 and Release|x64 build clean at `/W3` with `SDLCheck`.
- [ ] Token-normalized `NotepadPanel.cpp` matches the pre-refactor logic (only theme deltas allowed).
- [ ] All previously exported symbols still exported; new symbols added; nothing removed.
- [ ] App launches, tabs/editor/search/toolbar/menus behave as before.
- [ ] Dark default unchanged pixel-for-pixel for embedders.
- [ ] `NP_THEME_SYSTEM` follows Windows light/dark live (`WM_SETTINGCHANGE`).
- [ ] `.vcxproj.filters` lists every file; no orphan `#pragma comment(lib)` remains.
- [ ] `grep -c '// Close the current block'` = 0; `grep -c '// ===='` = 0.

---

## Decisions I will take unless you say otherwise

1. **Embedded default = Dark**, standalone app = System (backwards compatible).
2. **Add PCH** (reference convention) — moved defines live in `pch.h`.
3. **Do not split** `NotepadPanel.cpp` into multiple translation units yet; the module-layout rule is documented and the file is organised into reference-style sections. Splitting is a separate, higher-risk refactor.
4. **No public API breakage** — theme modes are additive; `SetTheme`/`GetTheme` keep their signatures.

# Win32 C++ style guide

Neage Notepad targets C++20 and the Windows SDK. These rules follow the NEWAGEAI
application and the NEWAGEWIN32UI control layout. They apply to every file in
this repository.

## Source layout and naming

- Keep one public module API in its matching `.h` file and its non-inline
  implementation in the matching `.cpp` file. Use `#pragma once` and include
  `"pch.h"` first in every project `.cpp` file.
- Place a module in its own directory when it owns more than one file:
  `Theme/Theme.h`, `Theme/Theme.cpp`. The panel host stays at the repository
  root because `NotepadPanel.h` is the published embedding contract.
- Use `PascalCase` for types and public functions, `camelCase` for parameters
  and locals, `m_` for members, `g_` for process globals, `s_` for file statics,
  and a `k` prefix for named constants.
- Keep the `NP_` prefix on everything that crosses the public C boundary.
- Include the header that directly declares each dependency. Keep project
  headers before standard-library headers. Source files are Unicode and use
  `W`-suffixed Win32 APIs with UTF-16 strings.
- Use four spaces, braces on their own line, and one statement per line.
  `.clang-format` and `.editorconfig` hold the editor defaults.

### Module tiers

Follow the NEWAGEWIN32UI split when a module wraps a control:

```
Controls/Standard/    common-control wrappers (edit, list, status, tab, ...)
Controls/Advanced/    owner-drawn or multi-part controls (menu, split button, ...)
```

A wrapper owns its child `HWND`, is non-copyable, and destroys the child in
`Reset()`. The parent window stays responsible for routing notifications and
must outlive the wrapper. Modules that are not controls (theme, configuration,
persistence) live in their own top-level directory instead.

## Comments

- Write comments for public contracts, ownership and lifetime, required
  parent-window message handling, units, and non-obvious Win32 behaviour.
  Do not narrate each statement.
- Use `///` comments immediately above public types and APIs. State what the
  caller must provide, what the callee owns, and any thread or DPI constraint.
- Use concise `// ---- Section ----` headings for substantial implementation
  sections. Do not use `// =====` banners.
- Add a short inline comment only when it explains a non-obvious invariant or a
  Win32-specific reason, for example:

```cpp
// Ctrl+W closes the tab; the host keeps Ctrl+F4 for the frame.
case IDM_TAB_CLOSE:
```

```cpp
// EM_SETBKGNDCOLOR takes the colour in lParam; wParam must be zero.
SendMessageW(inst->hEdit, EM_SETBKGNDCOLOR, 0, inst->theme.BgApp);
```

- Keep comments accurate when the code changes. Prefer descriptive names and
  small functions over a comment that restates the line.

### What not to write

Comments that restate the statement add noise and rot quickly. All of the
following were removed from this codebase and must not come back:

```cpp
} // Close the current block.
return TRUE; // Report success to the caller.
if (!inst) return FALSE; // Continue this branch only when the state object is unavailable.
Palette t; // Declare t for use by this block.
t.BgApp = RGB(22, 22, 25); // Update the bg app field with the calculated value.
size_t p = path.find_last_of(L"\\/"); // Declare p and start with path.find_last_of(L"\\/").
```

If a block needs a signpost, name it:

```cpp
struct NotepadInstance
{
    // Window handles
    HWND hSelf = nullptr;
    HWND hParent = nullptr;

    // Documents
    std::vector<Document *> docs;
};
```

## Theme

- All colours come from `Theme/Theme.h`. No `RGB()` constant belongs in a paint
  function.
- A component stores a `ThemePalette` copy and reads it at paint time. It never
  caches brushes across a theme change; brushes are recreated and the window is
  invalidated.
- `ThemeMode::System` is resolved through `ResolveDarkMode()` at the moment the
  palette is needed. A component that reacts to live changes handles
  `WM_SETTINGCHANGE` with `lParam == L"ImmersiveColorSet"`.
- Child controls follow the mode through `ApplyControlTheme()`; top-level frames
  call `ApplyTitleBarTheme()`. The embedded panel does not touch the host frame.
- Layout metrics are expressed in 96-DPI units and converted with
  `ScaleMetric(value, dpi)`. Font sizes are points and use `MulDiv(size, dpi, 72)`.

## Ownership and errors

- Treat every Win32 handle as either owned or borrowed. An owning wrapper is
  non-copyable and movable; `Reset()` destroys the owned resource and `Release()`
  transfers it. Never destroy a borrowed handle.
- The panel owns its child windows, fonts, brushes, and the instance record. The
  host owns the panel window itself and must call `DestroyNotepadPanel` before
  destroying its own window.
- Validate parameters at public boundaries. Return `bool` for success/failure,
  `std::optional` where an empty value differs from failure, and document when a
  function returns a native Win32 previous-state/index value.
- Callbacks fired from the panel are synchronous. A callback must not destroy the
  panel from inside the notification; post a message instead.

## Adding a module

1. Create `Module/Module.h` with the public contract only: enums, structs, and
   `///`-documented function declarations. No implementation details, no
   `static` helpers.
2. Create `Module/Module.cpp`, starting with `"pch.h"` and then the module
   header, followed by `// ---- Name ----` sections.
3. Keep the module free of dependencies on `NotepadPanel.h`. Convert types at the
   boundary instead, so the module stays reusable by the host application.
4. Register both files in `Neage Notepad.vcxproj` and add them to a matching
   filter in `Neage Notepad.vcxproj.filters`.
5. Document the module in `README.md` and, when it changes the embedding
   surface, in `NOTEPAD_PANEL_API.md`.
6. Build `Debug|x64` and `Release|x64` before committing.

## Example API documentation

```cpp
/// Returns the palette for a concrete light/dark decision.
/// The caller owns the returned value; no GDI objects are created here.
ThemePalette GetPalette(bool dark) noexcept;

/// Applies the immersive dark caption to a top-level window.
/// Safe to call before the window is shown; ignored on systems without DWM.
void ApplyTitleBarTheme(HWND hwnd, bool dark) noexcept;
```

## Build integration

- Every `.cpp` implementation is listed in `Neage Notepad.vcxproj`; headers and
  sources also appear under a filter in `Neage Notepad.vcxproj.filters`.
- Link Win32 dependencies through the project settings
  (`comctl32.lib`, `comdlg32.lib`, `shell32.lib`, `dwmapi.lib`, `uxtheme.lib`)
  rather than source-level `#pragma comment(lib, ...)`.
- The Common Controls v6 dependency is declared in the project manifest
  settings, not with a linker pragma.
- Request the `ICC_*` initialization flags before creating a common control.

### Theme

#### `NPTheme` struct
```cpp
typedef struct NPTheme {
    COLORREF bgApp;        // main editor background
    COLORREF bgPanel;      // tab bar / toolbar / status bar
    COLORREF bgCard;       // active tab / search input
    COLORREF bgBtn;        // chip buttons
    COLORREF bgBtnHi;      // pressed buttons
    COLORREF border;       // strong borders
    COLORREF borderSoft;   // subtle separators
    COLORREF textHi;       // primary text
    COLORREF textMid;      // secondary text
    COLORREF textLow;      // disabled text
    COLORREF accent;       // accent (active tab underline)
    COLORREF selBg;        // selection highlight
    COLORREF iconIdle;     // icon default
    COLORREF iconActive;   // icon hover/active
} NPTheme;
```

#### `SetTheme`
```cpp
BOOL SetTheme(HWND hPanel, const NPTheme* theme);
```
Applies a custom color palette. Pass NULL to revert to the default dark theme.
Also updates RichEdit background and text color for all tabs. Triggers a full
repaint.

#### `GetTheme`
```cpp
BOOL GetTheme(HWND hPanel, NPTheme* outTheme);
```
Reads the current theme palette.

#### Light theme example
```cpp

    .bgPanel    = RGB(248, 248, 248),
    .bgCard     = RGB(238, 238, 238),

    .selBg      = RGB(206, 224, 255),
    .iconIdle   = RGB(60, 60, 68),
    .iconActive = RGB(20, 20, 28),
};

```

---

## 11. Theme Coordination

### 11.1 Default Theme

The built-in dark theme (current `Theme::Palette`) is the default. It is copied into each `NotepadInstance` at creation time.

### 11.2 Custom Theme

`SetTheme(hPanel, &theme)` copies the provided palette into the instance and triggers a full repaint. Every paint function (`PaintTabs`, `PaintSearchBar`, `PaintStatusBar`, `DrawButton`, icon drawing) reads from `instance->theme` instead of the global `Theme::` namespace.

### 11.3 Light Theme Support

The color set is already well-structured (14 named colors). A light theme is just a different `NPTheme` struct:

```cpp
NPTheme light = {
    .bgApp      = RGB(255, 255, 255),
    .bgPanel    = RGB(248, 248, 248),
    .bgCard     = RGB(238, 238, 238),
    .bgBtn      = RGB(228, 228, 230),
    .bgBtnHi    = RGB(218, 218, 222),
    .border     = RGB(200, 200, 204),
    .borderSoft = RGB(220, 220, 224),
    .textHi     = RGB(28, 28, 32),
    .textMid    = RGB(100, 100, 108),
    .textLow    = RGB(150, 150, 158),
    .accent     = RGB(37, 99, 235),
    .selBg      = RGB(206, 224, 255),
    .iconIdle   = RGB(60, 60, 68),
    .iconActive = RGB(20, 20, 28),
};
SetTheme(hPanel, &light);
```

### 11.4 RichEdit Theme

`SetWindowTheme(hEdit, L"DarkMode_Explorer", nullptr)` is called for dark mode. For light mode, call `SetWindowTheme(hEdit, L"Explorer", nullptr)` and set `EM_SETBKGNDCOLOR` to the theme's `bgApp`.

### 11.5 DWM Dark Title Bar

`DwmSetWindowAttribute(hwnd, 20, &dark, sizeof(dark))` is only called by the standalone exe wrapper, not by the DLL. In embedded mode the host owns the title bar and is responsible for its own dark/light appearance.

edits.newText:
### 11.1 Theme Module

`Theme/Theme.h` owns the palette model. `ThemeMode` is `System`, `Light`, or `Dark`; `ThemePalette` holds the 15 colours the panel paints with. `GetPalette(bool)` returns a built-in palette, `ResolveDarkMode(ThemeMode)` collapses a mode to a decision, and `IsSystemDarkMode()` reads `AppsUseLightTheme` from the current user's personalization key.

Each `NotepadInstance` stores a `ThemePalette`, the requested `ThemeMode`, and the resolved `darkMode` flag. Panels start in `NP_THEME_DARK`, which preserves the palette the library always shipped; the standalone exe selects `NP_THEME_SYSTEM` after creating its panel.

### 11.2 Custom Theme

`SetTheme(hPanel, &theme)` copies the provided palette into the instance and triggers a full repaint. Every paint function (`PaintTabs`, `PaintSearchBar`, `PaintStatusBar`, `DrawButton`, icon drawing) reads from `instance->theme`; nothing reads a global palette. `SetTheme(hPanel, NULL)` restores the palette of the instance's current mode.

A custom palette is not tied to a Windows mode, so the Rich Edit and scrollbar styling is derived from the background luminance (`IsDarkPalette`). Custom palettes are not overwritten by `WM_SETTINGCHANGE`; changing the mode discards them.

### 11.3 Built-in Light Palette

`LightPalette()` in `Theme/Theme.cpp` returns the light colour set; `SetThemeMode(hPanel, NP_THEME_LIGHT)` applies it. Hosts that need different colours keep using `SetTheme` with their own `NPTheme`.

### 11.4 RichEdit Theme

`ApplyControlTheme(hwnd, darkMode)` selects `DarkMode_Explorer` or `Explorer`, and the panel pushes `EM_SETBKGNDCOLOR` plus `CFM_COLOR` for every document when the palette changes. The inline rename editor and both search fields use the same call.

### 11.5 DWM Dark Title Bar

`ApplyTitleBarTheme(hwnd, dark)` is only called by the standalone exe wrapper, not by the panel. In embedded mode the host owns the title bar and is responsible for its own dark/light appearance. The panel reacts to a forwarded `WM_SETTINGCHANGE` (`lParam == L"ImmersiveColorSet"`) when its mode is `NP_THEME_SYSTEM`.

# Neage Notepad

A tabbed Windows notepad built with native Win32 C++20 and no UI framework. The
editor is a Rich Edit 4.1 control hosted by a panel window that can run either
inside this executable or embedded in a host application.

## Files

```
NotepadPanel.h            public C API for embedding the panel
NotepadPanel.cpp          panel window, tabs, toolbar, search, menus, exports
NEWAGENOTEPADMain.cpp     standalone frame window and message loop
Theme/Theme.h             theme modes, palettes, DPI and Win32 theming contract
Theme/Theme.cpp           palette tables, registry lookup, DWM and uxtheme calls
pch.h / pch.cpp           precompiled header (NOMINMAX, WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN)
resource.h / app.rc       icon resource
WIN32_CPP_STYLE.md        ownership, naming, and comment conventions
NOTEPAD_PANEL_API.md      API reference for embedders
EMBEDDING_SPEC.md         design notes and integration contract
.clang-format             formatter profile
.editorconfig             whitespace and encoding defaults
Neage Notepad.vcxproj     MSBuild project and Win32 library links
```

## Build

Open `Neage Notepad.vcxproj` in Visual Studio 2022 (Desktop development with
C++), select `x64` / `Debug`, and press F5. Command-line equivalent:

```
msbuild "Neage Notepad.vcxproj" -p:Configuration=Release -p:Platform=x64
```

The executable compiles `NotepadPanel.cpp` with `NOTEPAD_PANEL_STATIC`. To build
the panel as a DLL, set `NOTEPAD_PANEL_EXPORTS` and link `NotepadPanel.lib`.

## Theme

`Theme/Theme.h` is the single source of colour and DPI decisions:

```cpp
#include "Theme/Theme.h"

const bool dark = ResolveDarkMode(ThemeMode::System);
ApplyTitleBarTheme(hwnd, dark);        // top-level frames only
ApplyControlTheme(hwndEdit, dark);     // Rich Edit and inline editors
```

The panel exposes the same model through its C API:

```cpp
SetThemeMode(hPanel, NP_THEME_SYSTEM);   // System, Light, or Dark
SetThemeMode(hPanel, NP_THEME_LIGHT);
```

Panels start in `NP_THEME_DARK` so an existing host keeps the original look. The
standalone application selects `NP_THEME_SYSTEM` and forwards
`WM_SETTINGCHANGE` (`lParam == L"ImmersiveColorSet"`) so the editor follows the
Windows app theme live. A host palette applied with `SetTheme` is kept until the
mode changes.

## Reusable modules

Every non-panel component follows the NEWAGEWIN32UI layout: one public header
with the contract, one `.cpp` with the implementation, registered in
`.vcxproj` and `.vcxproj.filters`.

```
Module/Module.h       enums, structs, ///-documented declarations
Module/Module.cpp     "pch.h", then the module header, then // ---- sections
```

Control wrappers use the `Controls/Standard` (common controls) and
`Controls/Advanced` (owner-drawn or multi-part) split. A wrapper owns its child
`HWND`; the parent window must outlive it and still routes notifications.
Modules must not depend on `NotepadPanel.h` — convert types at the boundary
instead, as `NotepadPanel.cpp` does with `NPTheme`.

See [WIN32_CPP_STYLE.md](WIN32_CPP_STYLE.md) for the comment rules, ownership
rules, and the full module checklist.

static void RefreshTheme(NotepadInstance *inst)

edits.oldText: In embedded mode the host owns the title bar and is responsible for its own dark/light appearance. The panel reacts to a forwarded `WM_SETTINGCHANGE` (`lParam == L"ImmersiveColorSet"`) when its mode is `NP_THEME_SYSTEM`.
edits.newText:
In embedded mode the host owns the title bar and is responsible for its own dark/light appearance. The panel reacts to a forwarded `WM_SETTINGCHANGE` (`lParam == L"ImmersiveColorSet"`) when its mode is `NP_THEME_SYSTEM`.

A mode change is reported to the host as `NP_NOTIFY_THEME_CHANGED` (`WM_NOTIFY`, `nmhdr.code == 9`). content.text:
Fixed and verified. There were three independent causes — the screenshot showed them exactly: caption `22,22,25` and toolbar `30,30,34` stayed dark while the tab strip and editor went light.

## 1. Toolbar never repainted

`RefreshTheme` only invalidated the panel window:

```cpp
InvalidateRect(inst->hSelf, nullptr, TRUE);
```

Child windows own their paint regions, so the toolbar host, its owner-draw buttons, and the search fields kept the previous palette forever. Now:

```cpp
const UINT flags = RDW_INVALIDATE | RDW_ERASE | RDW_ALLCHILDREN | RDW_UPDATENOW;
RedrawWindow(inst->hSelf, nullptr, nullptr, flags);
RedrawWindow(inst->hToolbarHost, nullptr, nullptr, flags);
```

The cached `WM_CTLCOLOR*` brushes are also destroyed, since they carried the old colours.

## 2. Title bar never updated

The panel fired `NP_NOTIFY_THEME_CHANGED`, but the app created the panel with `notifyProc = nullptr` and had no `WM_NOTIFY` handler — and `ApplyChromeTheme` resolved the compile-time startup mode instead of the panel's current one. Now the frame handles the notification and asks the panel:

```cpp
case WM_NOTIFY:
    if (reinterpret_cast<const NMHDR *>(lParam)->code == NP_NOTIFY_THEME_CHANGED)
        ApplyChromeTheme();
...
const int mode = g_hPanel ? GetThemeMode(g_hPanel) : kThemeMode;
ApplyTitleBarTheme(g_hFrame, ResolveDarkMode(static_cast<ThemeMode>(mode)));
```

## 3. Menus could keep dark corners

The popup was clipped to a rounded shape but only the *inner* rounded card was filled, so everything outside that fill kept whatever was on screen before — including a previous dark menu at the same position. Now the whole client rect is filled and the rounding comes from a window region:

```cpp
FillSolid(hdc, rc, inst->theme.BgCard);
HRGN region = CreateRoundRectRgn(0, 0, maxW + 1, totalH + 1, radius * 2, radius * 2);
SetWindowRgn(inst->menuWnd, region, FALSE);
```

An open menu is also invalidated by `RefreshTheme`.

## Verification

I instrumented a temporary build to render its own window to a bitmap, then switched themes **after** the window had painted:

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Dark → Light at runtime | **0 of 279,278** sampled pixels matched any dark palette colour; caption white, toolbar `248,248,248`, tab strip and status bar `248,248,248` |
| Light → Dark at runtime | All surfaces dark; the only light pixels are the dark theme's `IconActive` white icon highlights |
| Builds | `Debug/Release × x64/Win32` — zero warnings |
| Launch | Release binary starts and stays alive |

Changed: [NotepadPanel.cpp](D:\CPROJECTS\NEAGENOTEPAD\NotepadPanel.cpp) (`RefreshTheme`, menu paint + region), [NEWAGENOTEPADMain.cpp](D:\CPROJECTS\NEAGENOTEPAD\NEWAGENOTEPADMain.cpp) (`WM_NOTIFY`, chrome resolution), [EMBEDDING_SPEC.md](D:\CPROJECTS\NEAGENOTEPAD\EMBEDDING_SPEC.md) (hosts are told to re-theme their frame on `NP_NOTIFY_THEME_CHANGED`). The verification scaffolding was removed before the final build.
